keyEvents.impact: Millions starved; anchors a national memory of Russian imperial domination and existential threat
Over 90% voted for independence; Ukraine emerged with the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal

keyEvents.event: Budapest Memorandum: nuclear arsenal surrendered for security assurances
keyEvents.impact: Assurances proved worthless in 2014 and 2022; drives today's insistence on binding guarantees

keyEvents.event: Maidan revolution, Russian annexation of Crimea and war in Donbas
keyEvents.impact: Pro-European turn cost territory; eight years of frozen war built a Western-trained army

keyEvents.event: Russian full-scale invasion repelled from Kyiv; Kharkiv and Kherson counteroffensives
keyEvents.impact: National survival against the odds made resistance the core of identity and earned EU candidate status
War settled into attritional drone-dominated trench warfare; Russia regained initiative
First foreign occupation of Russian soil since 1941; reversed by Russian and North Korean troops in 2025

keyEvents.event: Oval Office clash, US minerals deal and the 28-point peace plan
keyEvents.impact: Dependence on a transactional Washington; Europe's EUR 90bn loan became the main financial lifeline

keyEvents.event: Trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks stall over Donbas; local Oleshky ceasefire
keyEvents.impact: Kyiv refuses to cede the rest of Donetsk without a referendum; war of attrition continues under martial law

history.narrative: A nation forged in war, fighting for survival against a far larger neighbor while about a fifth of its land is occupied. Mobilized society, drone innovation and Western money keep it in the fight, but manpower, an exhausted grid and dependence on fickle partners define its limits.

redLines.description: Legal recognition of Russian sovereignty over occupied territories or withdrawal from unoccupied Donetsk without a referendum
Imposed neutrality, caps on the army or a ceasefire without enforceable Western security guarantees
A renewed northern offensive on Kyiv from Belarusian territory

internalDivisions.name: War fatigue and mobilization resentment versus fight-to-victory camp
Anti-corruption institutions versus presidential office power (Yermak/Energoatom scandal)
Front-line east and south versus relatively safe west; displaced millions

goals.description: Survive as a sovereign state and hold the front line against Russian offensives
Secure binding Western security guarantees (NATO or coalition-of-the-willing troops) before any ceasefire
Never legally cede occupied land; restore territorial integrity over the long term
Keep the economy and energy grid alive with EU financing and advance EU accession
